title: Link worker social prescribing: an umbrella review of wellbeing, loneliness, consultation and cost outcomes with an overlap analysis
abstract: Objective: to summarise what systematic reviews show about link worker social prescribing once review quality and overlap are taken into account. Design: umbrella review of reviews published from 2017, with AMSTAR 2 appraisal, a citation matrix and GRADE per outcome. Results and conclusions will be written after the synthesis.
introduction: Reviews of social prescribing reach conflicting conclusions and draw heavily on the same small evaluations. Commissioners need an account that counts each primary study once.
methods: Four databases and two registers were searched for reviews from January 2017. Reviews were appraised with AMSTAR 2; a citation matrix and the corrected covered area measured overlap; each outcome was graded separately.
results: No reviews have been screened yet. The report will present the review flow, appraisal, the citation matrix, and outcome-level findings with certainty.
discussion: The discussion will explain disagreements between reviews through overlap and study design and set out what the evidence supports for funding decisions.
limitations: Dependence on existing reviews, a single main reviewer, and published data only.
conclusion: To be written after the synthesis.
reportingChecklist: PRIOR with PRISMA 2020 for the search
summary: PRIOR-structured draft with results left empty.
